messages:
maria (Support): Hey team — AcmeDocs reported SSO stopped working right after they rotated their IdP cert. They say users hit a login failure with a signature error. Customer report: 

acme-sre (customer): We rotated our cert in the IdP last night (Okta). After that users get an error when logging into Redwood. Old sessions still work. New logins fail with 'Signature verification failed'. We rolled back to the old cert in Okta and that fixed it temporarily. Can you confirm what's going on? :confused:

maria (Support): Thank you. I captured our gateway logs when they hit the SP endpoint. Here's the relevant error we see in the saml verifier: 

```
SAML lib error: Signature validation failed: no matching x509 certificate found for signature
Trace: saml.signature.verify -> KeySelector returned certificate with thumbprint != signature thumbprint
```

maria (Support): I also attempted to refresh the IdP metadata from their metadata URL (we cache it for 1h). The fetch returned 200 and the metadata file now has two <KeyDescriptor> entries. One includes the new cert, the other the old cert. 

acme-sre (customer): Right — Okta shows both certificates in the application: the new one is listed but we left the old cert as 'active' for a bit. We then switched the new cert to be default/primary, but users still saw failures until we explicitly re-saved the app settings. Weird.

jordan (eng-runtime): :eyes: Can you paste the IdP metadata (redacted) or the SAMLResponse (base64) so I can inspect the Assertion's Signature KeyInfo? Two quick theories: 1) our metadata parser is choosing the wrong KeyDescriptor (e.g., it picks the first KeyDescriptor and Okta put the encryption key first), 2) the IdP is signing with a cert that is present but missing use="signing" so our selector doesn't pick it.

maria (Support): Pasting a redacted SAMLResponse (customer provided):

```
<base64>SAMLPAYLOAD_REDACTED_FOR_PRIVACY_BASE64...</base64>
```

maria (Support): And the IdP metadata snippet we fetched (redacted):

```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://acme.okta.com/app/abcd">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor>
      <ds:KeyInfo>--CERT A (old) --</ds:KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="encryption">
      <ds:KeyInfo>--CERT B (new) --</ds:KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```

adeela (idp-team): Looks like the new cert (CERT B) has use="encryption" and the old one is missing a use attribute entirely. Some SAML libraries assume missing 'use' means signing, others pick first entry. If the IdP signed with CERT B but flagged it as 'encryption', our selector could skip it and try CERT A (which no longer matches). That would explain intermittent behavior when Okta reorders or when the app settings are re-saved.

jordan (eng-runtime): Agreed. Our current metadata selector logic (python-saml-wrapper) prefers KeyDescriptor with use="signing", otherwise falls back to first KeyDescriptor. If an IdP marks the signing cert as encryption, we'll miss it. Repro steps for us: 1) fetch metadata, 2) parse KeyDescriptor list order, 3) select X509Data by use or fallback. I can put together a quick patch to prefer KeyInfo subjectKeyIdentifier or compare cert fingerprints with the signature's KeyInfo (if present) before picking fallback.

maria (Support): For immediate mitigation, can we advise the customer to mark the new cert as 'Active' and re-save the app/integration in Okta so the metadata exposes the signing cert clearly? Also asking them to temporarily revert if needed (they already did that and it worked).

acme-sre (customer): We re-saved and it fixed it after a few minutes. We can keep the old cert as active for now until you confirm. We want a root cause so we can rotate properly.

jordan (eng-runtime): Action items: 
- I will add a small change to our metadata key selection to prefer explicit use="signing" and, if absent, try to correlate KeyInfo/X509Certificate fingerprint with the Signature's KeyInfo in the response before falling back to the first.
- Add additional logging around which cert fingerprint we tried vs the signature fingerprint.
- We'll also add a deploy-time test that parses a metadata file with mixed use attributes.

deploy-bot: Metadata refresh worker ran at 1748932175 and completed successfully (cache updated).

oncall-eng: @jordan please include me on the PR. If the change risks any behavior change we should stage it behind a feature flag and enable gradually.

adeela (idp-team): Also worth telling customers: when rotating certs in Okta, make the new cert 'Default' and re-save the app, and verify the metadata endpoint (append /metadata) contains a KeyDescriptor with use="signing" that includes the new certificate. If they can't get that, open an Okta support ticket — sometimes the UI doesn't propagate properly until the underlying app is re-saved.

maria (Support): I'll send AcmeDocs a summary and the short mitigation steps: re-save app, set new cert as default, revert if problem occurs. I'll file an internal bug for the runtime selection logic and link this thread. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

acme-sre (customer): Thanks folks, appreciate the quick triage. We'll hold on rotation until you confirm the runtime fix.

jordan (eng-runtime): Will post PR link here when ready. Expected ETA: small fix + canary in 48h.

maria (Support): Closing the support ticket once we confirm the patch. Keeping thread open for updates.
